## Research Profile

::: {custom-style="CVProfile"}
Mammal ecologist and evolutionary biologist integrating ecological and genomic data
to investigate evolutionary and biodiversity patterns. My research is centred on
African mammals — systematics, phylogeography, and conservation biology — alongside
an extensive, long-running collaboration on the mammals of Southeast Asia. I combine
field-collected specimen data with phylogenomic and macroecological analysis to
resolve species limits, reconstruct diversification histories, and quantify how
climatic and anthropogenic pressures shape mammal diversity across elevational and
ecoregional gradients.
:::

## Field Research Experience

::: {custom-style="CVLead"}
All campaigns were joint surveys of the National Museums of Kenya and the Kunming
Institute of Zoology, CAS, totalling 5,974 catalogued small mammal specimens.
Methods: Sherman live-trap and pitfall–drift-fence arrays on standardised elevational
transects; in situ external and cranial morphometrics; tissue sampling in 95% ethanol;
voucher preparation and accession into the NMK mammal collection.
:::

::: {.entry date="28 Sep – 14 Nov 2019"}
Cherang'any Hills, Mt. Elgon & Mathews Range · Kenya

854 rodents and shrews. Montane survey across three geographically isolated
highlands, targeting elevational gradients in western and northern Kenya.
:::

::: {.entry date="12 Aug – 14 Sep 2018"}
Mau Forests, Kakamega Forest & Yala Swamp · Kenya

1,450 rodents and shrews. Gradient from highland forest through Guineo-Congolian
lowland rainforest to wetland.
:::

::: {.entry date="9 Jan – 5 Feb 2018"}
Loita Hills forest ecosystem · Kenya

877 rodents and shrews. Dry montane forest isolated from other Kenyan highlands;
key data for comparative phylogeography of forest specialists.
:::

::: {.entry date="19 Aug – 22 Sep 2016"}
Chyulu Hills, Tsavo National Parks, Shimba Hills & Gongoni Forest · Kenya

861 rodents, shrews and bats. East–west transect from coastal forest to interior
savanna; first comprehensive small mammal survey at several sites.
:::

::: {.entry date="6 Sep – 13 Oct 2015"}
Mount Kenya — Chogoria and Sirimon transects · Kenya

1,932 rodents and shrews. Two-transect elevational survey from montane forest through
bamboo and moorland to alpine heath; the largest single-site small mammal dataset
from Kenya.
:::

::: {.entry date="Jul – Aug 2015"}
Loita Forest & Kakamega Forest National Reserve · Kenya

Forest-dependent small mammal communities in two contrasting forest types, with a
team led by Prof. Julian Kerbis Peterhans (Field Museum of Natural History /
Roosevelt University).
:::
